description: Tries + suffix structures decomposed. Standard trie for prefix lookup. Compressed trie / radix tree for space. Aho-Corasick for multi-pattern matching. Suffix tree + suffix array for substring queries. Each variant trades construction time, query time, and space for different patterns of use.

sub_mechanisms.name: trie_per_character_edge
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each node has child pointers indexed by character. Path from root to a node spells a prefix.
sub_mechanisms.why: O(m) lookup where m is key length. Independent of dictionary size. Used in autocomplete, spell-check, T9 predictive text. Space: O(σ · total_chars) where σ is alphabet size.

sub_mechanisms.name: trie_end_of_word_marker
sub_mechanisms.definition: Nodes carry a boolean (or value pointer): 'this prefix is itself a complete word'. Distinguishes 'inter' (prefix of 'interesting') from inserted 'inter'.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without it, you couldn't distinguish 'inserted as a key' from 'happens to be a prefix'. End-of-word marker is what makes a trie a set/map vs just a prefix structure.

sub_mechanisms.name: compressed_trie_radix
sub_mechanisms.definition: Merge single-child chains into one edge labelled with the substring. Reduces space dramatically when most strings share long prefixes.
sub_mechanisms.why: Original trie wastes space on long single-child chains (e.g., one rare word adds many nodes). Radix tree merges them. Used in IP routing tables (LPC, levelled radix trees), file system indexes.

sub_mechanisms.name: patricia_trie
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compressed binary trie: each non-leaf branches on a specific bit position. Used for IP routing, bit-string indexing.
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimal for binary alphabets. Each internal node tests one bit; path encodes the prefix bit-by-bit. Used in Linux kernel for IPv4/v6 routing tables.

sub_mechanisms.name: aho_corasick_automaton
sub_mechanisms.definition: Trie of patterns + failure links pointing to longest proper suffix that's also a prefix in the trie.
sub_mechanisms.why: Multi-pattern matching in O(text + total_pattern_length + matches). Find all occurrences of N patterns in one pass over text. Used in network IDS (Snort), grep -F, virus scanners.

sub_mechanisms.name: aho_corasick_failure_links
sub_mechanisms.definition: On mismatch, jump to the failure link: longest proper suffix of current state that's also a state. Continue matching from there.
sub_mechanisms.why: Generalisation of KMP's failure function to multiple patterns. Computed by BFS over the trie. Without failure links, multi-pattern matching would restart at root on each mismatch — O(text × patterns) instead of O(text).

sub_mechanisms.name: suffix_tree
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compressed trie of all suffixes of a string. Internal nodes represent shared prefixes; leaves represent suffixes (and their start positions).
sub_mechanisms.why: Substring queries in O(m). Build in O(n) (Ukkonen's algorithm). Used in bioinformatics (sequence analysis), substring search engines. Powerful but high constant + space (~20× input size).

sub_mechanisms.name: suffix_array
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sorted array of all suffix start positions of a string. Smaller + simpler than suffix tree.
sub_mechanisms.why: ~4× input space (vs ~20× for suffix tree). Sort-based construction is conceptually simple; O(n log² n) or O(n log n) algorithms. Search via binary search: O(m log n). Used in compression (BWT), bioinformatics.

sub_mechanisms.name: longest_common_prefix_LCP_array
sub_mechanisms.definition: Auxiliary array alongside suffix array: LCP[i] = length of longest common prefix between suffix at sa[i] and sa[i-1].
sub_mechanisms.why: Many suffix-array algorithms (longest repeated substring, range LCP queries) reduce to LCP queries. Built in O(n) given suffix array (Kasai's algorithm).

sub_mechanisms.name: trie_for_IP_routing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Routers store IP prefix → outgoing interface in a binary trie (or compressed variant). Longest prefix match: descend deepest matching node.
sub_mechanisms.why: IP routing tables have ~1M prefixes. Trie lookup is O(32) for IPv4 / O(128) for IPv6 in worst case. Real routers use hardware-accelerated tries (TCAM) for line-rate forwarding.

sub_mechanisms.name: trie_memory_overhead
sub_mechanisms.definition: Standard trie with σ-sized child arrays: O(σ) per node. For σ = 256 (bytes), 1 KB per node — wasteful for sparse children.
sub_mechanisms.why: Compact trie variants address this: hash-trie (lazy child map), array-mapped trie (variable-size children), compressed prefixes. Real-world tries use one of these to control memory.

derivation_rules.name: trie_lookup_independent_of_dictionary_size
if: a trie holds N words and lookup target has length m
derivation_rules.why: Path length depends only on target's length. Dictionary size affects space + tree width but not lookup time. The 'index-by-character' approach turns N-way comparison into m-way path traversal.

derivation_rules.name: compressed_trie_avoids_unary_chains
if: a trie has long single-child paths
then: compression merges them into edges with multi-char labels
derivation_rules.why: Rare strings (e.g., 'pneumonoultramicroscopic...') create deep chains in standard trie. Compression collapses them: one edge with the full substring. Space drops from O(total_chars) to O(num_distinct_branches + total_chars in labels).

derivation_rules.name: aho_corasick_processes_text_in_one_pass
if: patterns are pre-built into an Aho-Corasick automaton
then: all pattern occurrences are found in O(text + matches)
derivation_rules.why: Each character of text → one automaton transition. Failure links keep the work linear (each character is processed once, plus failure jumps that amortise). The breakthrough vs naive O(text × patterns) multi-search.

derivation_rules.name: suffix_array_smaller_than_suffix_tree
if: substring queries are needed but memory is constrained
then: suffix array's O(n) space outperforms suffix tree's O(n) but with smaller constant
derivation_rules.why: Suffix array: 4×n bytes (just integers). Suffix tree: 15-20×n bytes (nodes + pointers). Bioinformatics + search-engine indexes typically use suffix arrays + LCP for this reason.

derivation_rules.name: IP_routing_uses_trie_for_line_rate_lookup
if: routers must look up destination prefixes at line rate
derivation_rules.why: Hash table can't do longest-prefix-match (need to test all prefix lengths). Binary search on sorted prefixes is O(log n) but cache-unfriendly. Trie does LPM naturally + can be hardware-accelerated via TCAM. Industry standard for routing.
